# The appointments Hádēs made — and who is keeping them

Take Hádēs's stories in sequence. They are not episodes; they are appointments — and the modern trades are keeping them.

## At a Glance

- **Temple:** Hádēs
- **Pantheon:** Greek
- **Domain of influence:** Underworld, Wealth
- **Pattern seats:** 3
- **Sectors touched:** Society & Spirit · Energy & Natural World · Commerce & Governance
- **Strongest seat:** Funerary & Memorial Services
- **Series:** The Resonance Files, No. 186 of 546

## The Cycle, Read Forward

### Funerary & Memorial Services — through *The Seizure of Persephonē*

The Homeric Hymn to Demeter gives the underworld its founding story.  Persephonē, daughter of Demeter, was gathering flowers — roses, crocus, violets, and 'the wondrous narcissus, a trap planted by Zeus to please Hades' (5–15) — when the earth gaped and Hádēs burst up in his golden chariot 'with the consent of Zeus' and carried her down, 'weeping and crying aloud' (30–32).

The atlas states the seat in one line: *Lord of the underworld; the destination administered.* The story above is the long version of the same sentence. Industries do not invent their archetypes; they inherit them and call them best practice.

### Mining & Natural Resources — through *The Judges of the Dead*

What happens after the ferryman?  The developed tradition — later than Homer, who knows only the dreary meadow of Asphodel — gives the dead three judges: Minos, whom Homer already sees 'holding a golden scepter, dealing judgments among the dead' (Odyssey 11.

The atlas states the seat in one line: *Lord of the unseen wealth beneath the earth; mines are his treasury.* The story above is the long version of the same sentence. The trade thinks it is optimizing a process. It is re-enacting a charter.

### Finance, Wealth & Commerce — through *Orpheus and Eurydikē*

The musician Orpheus descended to bring back Eurydikē, bitten by a snake on her wedding day.  Vergil (Georgics 4.

The atlas states the seat in one line: *Plouton, the hidden wealth; underground value made divine.* The story above is the long version of the same sentence. That is the cycle working: story becomes duty, duty becomes trade.

## The Theme That Runs the Cycle

Hádēs appears rarely in Greek myth because his realm is separate from the world of the living — and the Greeks preferred it that way. His stories all concern the boundary: how Persephonē crossed it, how Orpheus almost crossed back, and why the door only opens inward.

## The Method, Stated Plainly

None of this is numerology. A seat exists only where the match can be argued from the deity’s documented domains and deeds — weighted, published, and falsifiable. The derivation, the weights, and the challenge process are public on the [methodology page](/patterns/methodology/). If a seat in this file reads wrong, the atlas itself tells you how to prove it — and the correction becomes part of the record.

## For the Ones Who Work There

If you work in funerary & memorial services, mining & natural resources, or any trade this temple holds a seat in, this is the honest version of what a placement means: your industry beside the story it has been re-telling all along — on the temple floor itself, before an audience that came specifically to read it. The [patron tier](/hades/patron/) and the [advertising terms](/terms/advertising/) describe the mechanics; the resonance above describes the fit.
